criteria.text: Diagnosis of one of the listed systemic fungal infections, supported by documentation from the patient medical record.
Dates of trial of at least one alternative antifungal medication submitted.
Appropriate baseline laboratory tests for liver assessment obtained.
No history of acute or chronic liver disease.
Box Warnings discussed with the recipient.

notes: Partial encoding of Alaska Medicaid Oral Nizoral (ketoconazole), 200 mg tablet; effective 2022-06-01. Approval criteria 1–5 encoded; documentation and laboratory appropriateness require manual verification.

Indications and usage (manual review): use only when other effective antifungal therapy is not available or tolerated and potential benefits outweigh potential risks. Listed systemic fungal infections are in patients who have failed or are intolerant to other therapies.
Fungal meningitis is excluded: Nizoral tablets should not be used because of poor penetration into cerebrospinal fluid.
Boxed warnings (BBW) and hepatic risk require review; baseline liver assessment, no acute or chronic liver disease history, and discussion of Box Warnings with the recipient are required.
Authorization (manual review): coverage may be approved for 1 month.
Dispensing and quantity limit (manual review): 30-day supply, no more than 2 tablets per day.

Trial dates, appropriate baseline liver labs, liver disease history and warning discussion are attestations; dates, lab values and medical records are not independently verified. No evaluate-linked alternatives.
